caption:
Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 72. key is G major, and scale is major. Intimate Acoustic Folk-Pop Ballad with fingerpicked steel-string guitar, upright piano and a late string swell, a father singing to his young daughter.
Global Emotional Progression: The track opens almost unaccompanied, a single fingerpicked guitar and the faint hum of a kitchen before dawn, the male lead close to the microphone and half speaking, tired rather than sad. The first verse stays at that whisper, adding only a soft upright piano and the brush of a shaker as the memory of a hard morning builds, then lightens the moment the child appears in the doorway. The pre-chorus is the first real lift, a swell of warm low strings and a single sustained note under the voice. The chorus opens rather than explodes, a gentle kick and brushed snare arriving with a low male harmony beneath the lead, honest and plain, the emotional admission of the song. The second verse pulls back to guitar and piano for the drawing, the smallest and most domestic passage of the record, and lets one high sustained string note hold under the final couplet. The second chorus is wider, with the harmony doubled and a cello underneath. The instrumental break is sixteen bars of solo piano over held strings, no percussion, the sound of a man sitting in a car outside work. The bridge drops to voice and a single piano, nearly spoken, the tempo feeling slower without changing, as he imagines her leaving, then builds steadily through the last two lines. The final chorus arrives with the full warm arrangement, strings, soft brass pad and a wordless high choir, lifting on the line about being found every day, and the post-chorus drops the drums entirely. The outro returns to the opening guitar alone, the voice almost at a whisper, ending on a long decaying reverb and the kettle sound from the top of the song.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: A grey kitchen at ten past six with the light not yet up, bare feet on a cold hallway floor, a child's crayon drawing of a house with seven windows folded into a coat pocket, a car park outside an office building, a drawer of saved paper, a hallway light left on, father and daughter montages, first dance films, birthday and anniversary videos, quiet family edits.
Sonics & Production Profile: Close, warm, small-room soundstage with the vocal forward and almost unprocessed. Natural acoustic polish: woody low end from upright bass and piano rather than synthetic sub-bass, generous midrange left intact, soft unhyped top end. Dynamics stay low and conversational in the verses and open gently rather than loudly in the choruses. Light room reverb on the instruments, with the lead vocal kept close and dry so every breath and consonant reads.

Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Male). A warm, lived-in baritone in his late thirties, unhurried and close to the microphone in the low register, opening into a grainier and slightly frayed tone as he lifts into his upper chest voice.
Vocal Style: Confiding and nearly spoken in the verses, sitting right on the microphone with audible breath and soft consonants, as though the song is being said to one person rather than performed. The pre-chorus tightens the phrasing and lifts in pitch. The chorus is open-throated and plain, carried on feeling rather than power, with the catch left in the voice instead of smoothed away. The bridge falls back almost to speech before the final build.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: A single low male harmony a third beneath the lead thickens each chorus. A soft wordless pad of female and child-register voices joins the final chorus for warmth and height. Airy unison doubles of the lead drift beneath the outro.
Vocal FX: Close and dry lead with a short plate reverb and no audible delay through the verses. A gentle slapback opens on the choruses. The outro vocal is washed in a long soft reverb tail that decays into the room sound.

Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: Fingerpicked steel-string acoustic guitar is the spine, present from the first bar to the last fade, moving from a bare thumb-and-finger pattern to full strummed chords in the final chorus. Upright piano enters under the first verse and carries the instrumental break and the bridge alone.
Secondary: Warm low strings swell beneath the pre-choruses and sustain through the choruses, with a solo cello line added in the second half. A soft kick and brushed snare keep time only in the choruses. Upright bass enters with the first chorus and holds the low end. A wordless high choir pad and a soft brass bed widen the final chorus only.
Groove & Foundation Progression: The intro has no percussion, only guitar and a faint room hum. The verses add a quiet shaker and the brush of a snare rim without a full beat. The pre-chorus removes percussion for one bar to make space for the string swell. The choruses bring a soft kick, brushed snare and upright bass at a restrained volume. The instrumental break is piano and strings with no percussion at all. The bridge drops every instrument but one piano. The final chorus returns with the fullest arrangement of the track, and the post-chorus strips the drums away again. The outro ends on solo guitar.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: A kettle click and a faint kitchen hum open and close the record. The scratch of a crayon on paper and the rustle of folding paper sit low under the second verse. A single sustained high string note holds under the last couplet of each verse. Soft reverse-guitar swells mark the transitions into the choruses. A distant door and quiet footsteps on a wooden floor are heard once beneath the first verse. The final note is a long guitar decay into room silence.
lyrics:
[intro]
The kettle clicks at ten past six,
The window's holding grey,
I'm counting up the things to fix
Before I drive away.

[verse]
I used to carry mornings like a crate I couldn't set down,
Keys in one hand, trouble in the other, both my shoulders down.
I kept a running total of the ways I came up short,
And I called that being careful, and I called that being tough.
Then a door came open slowly at the far end of the hall,
And two bare feet went running on a floor that's always cold.
You had your hair gone sideways and one sock up to your knee,
And you asked me if the morning had a plan for you and me.
You climbed up on the counter where you're never let to climb,
And you told me it was going to be a good one, this time.

[pre-chorus]
I had been hunting for my reasons
In the hardest hour of day,
Then a small voice in a doorway
Took the heavy part away.

[chorus]
Everybody thinks I saved you,
But I've got it upside down.
I was the one who went missing,
Standing right here, not around.
I was tired and I was quiet
And I called it getting by,
Till you found me in the hallway
At ten past six one day.

[verse]
You drew a house with seven windows and a door too small to use,
And a yellow sun above the roof the sky could never lose.
You gave the clouds a purple edge, you put a fence around the lawn,
And a man beside a little girl, and the man was holding on.
You held it up and waited there and watched me while I read,
And you said that I could keep it if I kept it by my bed.
So I folded up your masterpiece and slid it in my coat,
And it rode there through the whole long day, a small and folded note.
Nobody in that building knew the reason I could stand,
There was paper in my pocket with a sun you drew by hand.

[pre-chorus]
I had been hunting for my reasons
In the hardest hour of day,
Then a small voice in a doorway
Took the heavy part away.

[chorus]
Everybody thinks I saved you,
But I've got it upside down.
I was the one who went missing,
Standing right here, not around.
I was tired and I was quiet
And I called it getting by,
Till you found me in the hallway
At ten past six one day.

[instrumental]

[bridge]
One day this hall will be a city
And the door you open, yours alone,
And the feet that came out running to me
Will be running down a road of your own.
I'll be glad. I'll carry boxes.
I'll stand waving at the kerb.
And I'll keep a folded drawing
In my coat, the way I learned.
You won't know you ever did it,
You'll just think you grew up fine.

[chorus]
Everybody thinks I saved you,
But I've got it upside down.
You're the one who came and got me,
You're the reason I'm around.
I was tired and I was quiet
And I called it getting by,
Then you found me in the hallway,
And you find me every day.

[post-chorus]
Ten past six, the kettle clicking,
Grey light coming through the floor,
You found me in the hallway
And you don't even know.

[outro]
So sleep now, there's no hurry,
Let the morning do the rest.
You found a man who'd gone missing
And you walked him to the step.
And he isn't going back there,
Not while you still say his name.
